messages:
Ivy: dropping a new thread for rollout "traffic guardrails" micro-interactions. goal: make canary + A/B actions obvious without blowing up density. figma: figma.com/...
Marcus: nice — one immediate Q: how do we surface that a canary is "paused" vs "ended" in compact view? tiny glyphs get confusing. :eyes:
Ivy: idea: two-state badge on slice: small dot for active, small square for paused, both with accessible labels. hover/keyboard shows full state text "Paused (reason)".
Ruth: Pause reason must be in the aria-label and audit link in the details panel. e.g., aria-label="Canary 2% 1 Variant C 1 paused due to error spike". Keep it short.
Ken: For mobile, tap opens sheet with big buttons. We should avoid destructive actions on a single-tap. Suggest primary = View, secondary = Promote, destructive hidden in overflow. Long-press is risky.
Aisha: accessibility checklist: 1) each slice role=button, tabindex=0; 2) add aria-pressed for selected variant; 3) aria-live region to announce state changes like "Variant C increased to 10%"; 4) respects prefers-reduced-motion. Also confirm contrast of tiny state badges (aim 4.5:1).
Marcus: Copy debate: keep action label short in menu column. Options: "Promote", "Send more" (PM likes conversational), "Increase traffic". My vote: "Promote variant" for clarity when multiple variants exist.
Ivy: we'll go with "Promote variant" + tooltip "Increase traffic to this variant" in details panel. Menu label stays concise.
Ruth: rollback flow: proposal is a two-step confirm in the menu: click Rollback -> confirm modal with typed-confirm for prod namespaces. Non-prod shows modal + 8s undo toast. Also include a checkbox "also revert config changes" when relevant.
Ken: logging: toast should link to the deployment audit (clickable) and show a brief operation id. Make sure to surface disabled state if another operation is in-flight.
Aisha: screenreader flow when modal opens: set focus to modal heading, aria-describedby points to details + typed-confirm instructions. When undo toast appears, announce "Rollback completed. Undo available for 8 seconds" via aria-live polite.
Marcus: timeline history: add a compact vertical marker for major versions in expanded history; each marker is keyboard navigable. When you focus a marker, show a mini-audit summary (committer, time, delta). Avoid auto-applying historical states; only preview.
Ivy: preview vs apply: preview opens read-only snapshot banner "Previewing snapshot from Jun 2 - not live" with CTA Return to live. Apply requires explicit confirm and logs. Keyboard: 'k' moves between markers, 'p' previews, 'a' opens apply modal. We'll document the keyboard map.
Ruth: microcopy: prefer verbs for actions (Promote variant, Revert to snapshot). For in-line tooltips keep nouns+numbers (e.g., "v2.4 1 3%"). Localization note: avoid idioms in tooltips.
Ken: motion & performance: avoid animating the entire timeline when many slices change. Instead, animate only the changed slice with crossfade. Also lazy-load detailed metrics in mini-panel to keep gestures snappy.
Aisha: colorblind accessibility: don't rely on color alone for success/failure; include icons and text. For small badges add a tooltip text and aria-label. Also test focus ring visibility at 1x zoom and high-contrast mode.
Ivy: action items: - adopt small shape badges for active/paused/ended with clear aria-labels - Promote menu label = "Promote variant" + details tooltip - Rollback = menu -> modal; typed-confirm for prod, undo toast for non-prod + logs link - preview-only mode for history markers; explicit apply flow - keyboard map doc (k,p,a,Esc) - reduced-motion crossfade on single-slice delta - ensure contrast & colorblind-friendly icons - update Figma + component tokens + accessibility examples.
ui-bot: Design review requested by Ivy for `traffic-guardrails-compact`. Reviewers: Marcus, Ruth, Ken, Aisha. Deadline: 4 business days. :spiral_calendar: 
Ivy: thanks everyone 1 pushing updates to the figma and will tag engineering with implementation notes (aria examples, keyboard order, prefer-reduced-motion CSS). Ping here once you review tokens.
